Hi Audrey,

Appreciate the clarity — I pulled together a short checklist and an internal handoff diagram for escrow scenarios. I've attached:

- geo_erasure_acceptance_checklist_v1.pdf (concise artifacts + timestamps we provide)
- escrow_handoff_sequence.png (sequence diagram showing escrow accept/verify/confirm)
- tenant_deletion_playbook_v3.md (internal runbook; redacted for customer packet)

High-level notes:
- Accepted erasure = successful completion of the final purge job + replication drain completed + provenance audit record written.
- Evidence bundle we provide: deletion request id, purge job run id & job log excerpt (sha256), replication drift report, final object manifest (names hashed), and an attestation statement signed by Redwoods' platform operations.
- SLAs: Initial purge execution within 24 hours of request for standard platform; full cross-region propagation confirmation within 72 hours for tenants with active replicas. We can negotiate faster windows for Dedicated customers.
- Escrow: We only escrow a minimal metadata bundle (tenant id, retention timestamp, legal hold flag) under customer-signed escrow agreement. We do not escrow customer content without explicit contract language.

Two clarifying Qs for your auditors:
1) Do they require raw object names in evidence, or can we provide salted hashes?
2) Will a platform attestation + machine-generated logs satisfy the evidence, or do they need a notarized third-party confirmation?

If OK, I'll produce a customer-facing one-page acceptance criteria doc for your packet and schedule a quick walkthrough with Marco and your audit team.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Hi Marco / Audrey — jumping in with technical confirmations and proposed wording.

1) Salting/hashing: We provide SHA-256 hashes salted with a per-tenant salt (stored hashed) and include the salt fingerprint in the evidence bundle. Auditor can verify by recomputing salted hashes if we share the salt fingerprint and audit nonce. We avoid providing raw object keys.

2) Log retention: purge job logs and replication reports are retained in our audit log store for 18 months by default (we can extend to contractual 36 months). The evidence bundle we give customers includes the relevant job log excerpts and a manifest excerpt; the full logs remain in our internal audit index. We mark internal logs as read-only and include an index pointer in the bundle.

3) Escrow schema (redacted sample):
- tenant_id (string)
- escrow_initiated_at (timestamp)
- legal_hold_flag (boolean)
- escrow_expiry (timestamp)
- escrow_contact (email)

We'll attach a redacted JSON schema in the customer packet; for legal reasons we keep the escrow storage encrypted under KMS and with a customer-signed escrow agreement.

4) Proposed attestation wording (short):

"Redwood Inference hereby attests that, for tenant <redacted-tenant-id>, deletion operations described in this evidence bundle were completed on <timestamp> and resulted in removal of customer content from Redwood-managed object stores in the specified geo-zone. Supporting purge job logs, replication drain reports, and an object manifest (salted hashes) are provided. This attestation is issued by Redwood Inference operations under access controls and audit logging consistent with our SOC2 controls."

Next steps: Kimberly — can you produce the one-page customer acceptance doc using the checklist I referenced and include the redacted JSON escrow schema? I'll add the attestation wording and an internal pointer to the audit index in the final bundle.

Rishi
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
